question.:question/problem:
Which integral  expression gives the arc length of the curve $f(t)=\langle 4 \sin{\left(2 t \right)},\,4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)},\,t^{2}\rangle$
from  $t=0$ to $t=1?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find $f'(t)$ and $\|f'(t)\|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(4 \sin{\left(2 t \right)}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t^{2})\rangle \\  & =\langle 8 \cos{\left(2 t \right)},\,- 8 \sin{\left(2 t \right)},\,2 t\rangle \\ \|f'(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(2 t\right)^{2} + \left(- 8 \sin{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2} + \left(8 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4 t^{2} + 64 \sin^{2}{\left(2 t \right)} + 64 \cos^{2}{\left(2 t \right)}} \\  & =\sqrt{64 \left(\frac{t^{2}}{16} + \sin^{2}{\left(2 t \right)} + \cos^{2}{\left(2 t \right)}\right)} \\  & =\sqrt{4 t^{2} + 64}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is:

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\int_{0}^{1}\|f'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t=\int_{0}^{1}2 \sqrt{t^{2} + 16}\,\mathrm{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find $f'(t)$ and $\|f'(t)\|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(t) & =(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 e^{t}))\,i+(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(e^{t}))\,j+(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 t e^{t}))\,k \\  & =(2 e^{t})\,i+(e^{t})\,j+(3 t e^{t} + 3 e^{t})\,k \\ \|f'(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(3 t e^{t} + 3 e^{t}\right)^{2} + \left(e^{t}\right)^{2} + \left(2 e^{t}\right)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\left(t^{2} + 2 t + 1\right) 9 e^{2 t} + e^{2 t} + 4 e^{2 t}} \\  & =\sqrt{\left(9 t^{2} + 18 t + 1 + 4 + 9\right) e^{2 t}} \\  & =\sqrt{9 t^{2} + 18 t + 14} e^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\int_{1}^{2}\|f'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_{1}^{2}\sqrt{9 t^{2} + 18 t + 14} e^{t}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
